rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE, so this round raises obfuscation pressure across all seven passes while keeping cost weights calibrated to five11's profile: it is a tiny (1259 text bytes) bit-manipulation benchmark whose hot loops (read_x_bits, read_11_bits) are sensitive to per-iteration overhead, so BCF and IBR get the highest RuntimeCost weights (0.55/0.45) to limit their firing in tight loops, while FLA is favored slightly over BCF as it flattens control flow with lower steady-state overhead. SUB stays strongest overall — arithmetic substitution is nearly free here since the code is dominated by shifts/masks that substitute well, and its low cost weights let it apply broadly. SPLIT and IGV are cheap structural/graph transformations well suited to the 12 small functions, so their cost weights stay low to let them apply. ICALL keeps a moderate CorrectnessRisk weight (0.25) since indirect-call lowering on the small helper-heavy call graph is where residual correctness risk concentrates, even though round 1 was clean.
